full_judgment:
3. Basically, in this writ, the writ petitioner has challenged the propriety of the order dated 15-2-2017 passed by respondent No. 2, Adalat in Artha Execution Case No. 4 of 2014 through which the learned judge disposed of the execution case acting under section 33(9) of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain. The petitioner has also called in question the propriety of issuance of certificate issued under section 33(5) of the Ain in favour of decree-holder Bank issued on 15-2-2017 and sought a direction for providing him opportunity to pay the decreetal dues in installments under section 49 of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003. 

 The present respondent No. 4 as creditor filed a suit being Artha Rin suit No. 3 of 2013 before the said Artha Rin Adalat claiming an outstanding dues from the petitioner amounting to Taka 90,37,428. In the said suit, the petitioner did not appear consequent which, the suit was decreed ex-parte on 7-9-2014 for an amount of Taka 90,37,828 with interest to be payable by the petitioner at the rate of 12% of the decretal dues till realization of the same. Since as per the judgment, the petitioner did not come forward to repay the said amount, the creditor bank then filed an execution case being Artha Execution Case No. 4 of 2014 claiming an amount of taka 1,08,44,085. In furtherence of the said execution case, the decree-holder Bank then published auction notice under section 33(1) of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain on 16-3-2016 but on the very date no bid was dropped. Subsequently, the decree-holder bank published second auction notice on 18-5-2016 but at that time also no bidder came forward to purchase the mortgaged property resulting in, the Artha Rin Adalat on 5-1-2017 issued certified in favour of the Bank giving authority for holding possessing and enjoyment of the mortgaged property by the decree-holder under section 35(5) of the Ain, 2003. Thereafter, the learned judge disposed of the execution case under section 33(9) of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain. Barely 8 months of such disposal of the Artha Rin execution case, the petitioner on 23-1-2017 filed an application before the Artha Rin Adalat under section 49 of Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 seeking permission to pay decretal dues in 3 (three) years with 12 equal installments. However, without waiting for any order supposed to be passed on that very application by the Adalat, the petitioner straightaway came before this court and filed this writ petition challenging the propriety of the order passed by the Artha Rin Adalat disposing of the execution case under section 33(9) and that of the issuance of the certificate under section 33(5) of the Ain. 

 11. We have considered the submission so placed by the learned counsel for the petitioner and that of the respondent No.4. Only point revolves around in adjudicating the instant Rule whether any illegality has been committed by the Artha Rin Adalat in disposing of the execution case under section 33(9) of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain. On going through the order sheet in particular, the order passed by the Artha Rin Adalat in Artha Execution Case No.4 of 2014 (Annexure "C" series to the writ) in regard to publishing auction notice, I find that, on two consecutive occasions the auction notice was published fulfilling the legal requirement in issuing certificate provided in section 33(5) of the Ain and thus the Adalat disposed of the execution case under section 33(9) of the Ain. Since the point has already been decided by our Honb'le Appellate Division that after disposing of an execution case under section 33(9) of the Ain there has been no scope to entertain any application of the judgment-debtor to pay decreetal dues in installment so we are of the view that, the impugned order suffers from no material illegality and invariably instant writ petition bears no merit.
